Re: Appeal of adverse benefit determination  
Member: Cameron Brooks  
Member ID: W295648415  
Plan: Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield Commercial/ACA, Kentucky  
Reference number: POC-0948834B99-90261  
Requested service: C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion  
CPT: 22551  
Treating surgeon: Marchetti, MD

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my cervical fusion procedure. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document more than an adequate trial, as well as persistent and progressive neurologic impairment caused by a specific structural abnormality.

I have had progressive neck pain for 14 months. The pain has not been relieved by rest and has continued despite medication, injection treatment, and supervised physical therapy.

The submitted records document the following conservative treatment:

- Supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, for eight weeks from May 3, 2026, through June 28, 2026.
- Eighteen completed physical therapy visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAID treatment for four months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 5, 2026, which produced only two weeks of partial relief.

The conservative-treatment trial therefore was prolonged, supervised, and unsuccessful. Symptoms persisted despite these measures, and the injection produced only temporary partial improvement.

The clinical findings also establish a corresponding anatomic and neurologic problem. The June 29, 2026 MRI shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root. I have radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness. Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

The requested ACDF is directed at the documented C5-C6 lesion and the associated C6 nerve-root compression. It is not being requested for nonspecific neck pain alone. The records show persistent symptoms, failure of nonoperative treatment, objective imaging evidence, and a matching neurologic deficit.

The submitted records also document that there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a nonsmoker. These facts do not identify a clinical reason to delay or deny the requested procedure.

I also reviewed the publicly available Carelon spine-surgery material that appears potentially relevant to cervical decompression and fusion. That material discusses cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy, diagnostic confirmation, response to prior treatment, and failure of conservative management. However, the exact Anthem Kentucky commercial-plan policy applied to this determination has not been publicly confirmed, so I have not quoted the plan or attributed specific wording to it here. Please provide the exact policy or clinical review criteria, including the version effective on the date of this determination, if the appeal is not approved.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551 at the C5-C6 level. If additional information is required, please contact Marchetti, MD, or advise the surgeon promptly regarding any peer-to-peer review opportunity.

Please send the appeal determination and any applicable further-review instructions to me and to my treating surgeon.

Sincerely,

Cameron Brooks
